title: Enterprise Backend: Minimal APIs, Microsoft.Extensions.AI & SSE Streaming
description: Build the production .NET 9 backend: asynchronous Minimal APIs, Microsoft.Extensions.AI pipeline middleware, Server-Sent Events (SSE) token streaming, resilient fallback routing, and MCP server endpoints.

data.text: Production Minimal APIs for Streaming AI

The backend of EnterpriseNexus is powered by .NET 9 Minimal APIs. In AI applications, user perceived performance hinges on Time to First Token (TTFT). Buffering an entire 800-word response produces 4–8 seconds of blank screen, whereas streaming tokens via Server-Sent Events (SSE) delivers the first word in under 350 milliseconds. We implement a non-buffering HTTP/2 SSE streaming endpoint powered by Microsoft.Extensions.AI and C# 13 asynchronous streams.

data.caption: Backend Streaming Pipeline with Middleware and Multi-Model Fallback
data.code:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Client as React 19 Frontend
    participant API as Minimal API Endpoint
    participant MW as Microsoft.Extensions.AI Pipeline
    participant Cache as Redis Semantic Cache
    participant LLM1 as Primary (Azure OpenAI)
    participant LLM2 as Resilient Fallback (Ollama / Local)

    Client->>API: POST /api/chat/stream (SSE)
    API->>MW: CompleteStreamingAsync(messages)
    MW->>Cache: Check Semantic Similarity (>0.96)
    alt Cache Hit
        Cache-->>MW: Return Cached Stream
        MW-->>API: Yield Cached Tokens
        API-->>Client: Stream SSE Events
    else Cache Miss
        MW->>LLM1: Stream Tokens (gpt-4o)
        alt Rate Limit (429) or Service Outage (503)
            LLM1-->>MW: Polly Circuit Breaker Trips
            MW->>LLM2: Fallback Stream (Llama 3.3)
            LLM2-->>MW: Token Stream
        else Normal Operation
            LLM1-->>MW: Token Stream
        end
        MW-->>API: IAsyncEnumerable<ChatResponseUpdate>
        API-->>Client: data: {"token":"...","citations":[...]}\n\n
    end

data.text: Using `Microsoft.Extensions.AI`, we compose the chat client as a modular middleware chain. Telemetry, caching, resilience, and function invocation wrap the underlying provider cleanly.

data.title: Program.cs Chat Client Composition
data.content: This pipeline configures Azure OpenAI with semantic caching, OpenTelemetry tracing, and circuit-breaker resilience.

data.text: The Minimal API endpoint streams JSON event payloads line-by-line using `Response.BodyWriter` with zero intermediate allocation.

data.title: SSE Streaming Minimal API Endpoint
data.content: Flushing tokens immediately with CancellationToken support to cancel upstream LLM requests when the user closes their browser.

data.title: CancellationToken Propagation Saves Cost
data.content: Always pass the `HttpContext.RequestAborted` CancellationToken to `CompleteStreamingAsync`. When users navigate away or hit 'Stop Generating', propagating the token immediately terminates the Azure OpenAI billable generation.

data.text: EnterpriseNexus exposes its internal services as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, allowing external AI agents (like Claude Desktop or IDE assistants) to query its corporate knowledge base securely.

data.title: MCP Tool Registration in ASP.NET Core
data.content: Exposing the hybrid search engine as a standardized JSON-RPC MCP tool.

data.title: Backend Implementation Quality Checklist
items: Endpoint uses HTTP/2 SSE with text/event-stream content type and disabled response buffering
CancellationToken from HttpContext wired through to IChatClient to eliminate phantom compute bills
Microsoft.Extensions.AI middleware pipeline includes Logging, OpenTelemetry, and Caching
Resilience pipeline configured with Polly for 429 RateLimit and 503 ServiceUnavailable fallbacks
Rate limiting policy enforced per tenant/user using Redis sliding-window counter
MCP endpoints adhere to the official Model Context Protocol JSON-RPC specification

data.title: Summary & Next Steps
points: Minimal APIs deliver high-throughput, low-allocation streaming for enterprise AI.
Microsoft.Extensions.AI provides a standard pipeline pattern for observability, caching, and tools.
Propagating cancellation tokens prevents wasteful token generation upon user disconnection.
Next, we build the React 19 streaming frontend with citations and tool approval flows.
data.takeaway: In generative AI systems, streaming is an engineering requirement, not a cosmetic feature: design for sub-second TTFT and immediate upstream cancellation.
